axioms: An identity change (name/URL/key) is only complete when every system that stores a copy of the old identity has been updated or reliably redirects — a plan is not proof of completion until each store is enumerated.
External namespaces (npm registry, GitHub) are owned by parties outside this repo and can silently reject or redirect a rename regardless of what the plan intends.
A grep-and-replace sweep is only as complete as its scope; anything outside the swept repos (other repos, other machines' local config) is a blind spot by default.
Settings/permission keys that reference a tool or plugin by name are load-bearing identity references just like code imports, even though they live in config rather than source.
A directory move and a git remote URL update are two separate operations; either can succeed while the other silently fails or lags.
Ordering matters: renaming the canonical repo before all consumers have moved leaves a window where some machine or config points at a dead identity.
A version bump landing in the same commit as an identity rename compounds two independent risks (wrong content published, or published under a colliding name) into one atomic, hard-to-bisect event.
primitives: GitHub repo URL and redirect behavior
git remote configuration and worktree linkage
failure_mode: Treats a rename as complete once the plan's named files are edited, without checking external registries (npm/GitHub) for collision or actual redirect behavior.
Misses config in repos/files not named in the plan's rename-sweep scope (e.g. an unlisted settings.local.json permission entry).
Doesn't notice when a directory-move step and a git-remote-update step could land out of order or partially.
Overlooks in-flight branches/worktrees that haven't yet merged to the branch a later rename step assumes is canonical.
